body:
> The AudioStreamSynchronized class came in 9 months ago from this PR #64488 from @reduz where there's a very extensive discussion about the features other than this one.
> 
> They've chosen to implement it with a fixed size array [Ref<AudioStreamPlayback> playback[AudioStreamSynchronized::MAX_STREAMS]](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/modules/interactive_music/audio_stream_synchronized.h#L89C2-L89C73) and a `stream_count` value to state the working size of the array.
> 
> This code seems to have been made in a hurry, as shown by the fact that the [class parameters](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/modules/interactive_music/audio_stream_synchronized.h#L91C1-L100C1)
> 
> ```c++
> int play_order[AudioStreamSynchronized::MAX_STREAMS];
> 
> double stream_todo = 0.0;
> int fade_index = -1;
> double fade_volume = 1.0;
> int play_index = 0;
> double offset = 0.0;
> 
> int loop_count = 0;
> ```
> 
> have been accidentally pasted in from `class AudioStreamPlaybackPlaylist` and are not used! So it's reasonable to expect shortcuts to have been taken, such as resetting all the streams when there has been a change.
> 
> Unfortunately there's also a bug: when you increase `stream_count` so it accesses more slots of the `playback` array, nothing gets reset even if there are valid streams in those slots. This gives you a sneaky backdoor of setting `stream_count` to zero, changing a sync stream, and then setting `stream_count` back to its original value.
> 
> [These loops over `playbacks`, which generally has one element, are really confusing and made me think there were more bugs than there were.]
> 
> This fix looks good, and I've even tested it out.
> 
> I have the following quibbles:
> 
>     1. Should you call `playback_sync->playback[p_stream_index].unref()` before you set it to the new `p_stream` value?
> 
>     2. If `set_stream_count()` increases the `stream_count`, should we initiate the playbacks and playing_pos of any non-null slots in the array of streams?  (Similarly, should we unref() the extra ones when `stream_count` decreases?)
> 
>     3. How are looping tracks managed?  Perhaps we need a global playback position that you use to set the play positions of any looping tracks modulo their length?  This would give a handy way to unroll loops on tracks should you not want to watch their  `loop_count` value, especially if the AudioStreamSynchronized also maintained its own global_length.

whoa, things made a lot more sense now, thanks for the observations!
i found a bug which was happening because of those loops over playbacks - if a stream was set to null and then the same index reset it to the previous value, it'd just ignore.
anyway, i started refactoring in order to make this fix work properly - also added [this fix](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/100292).
as for the things you pointed out:
1. done that after refactoring!
2. yea, i think stream_count variable should only have a getter and be set only privately - maybe add an 'add_sync_stream(index, stream)' and 'remove_sync_stream(index)' method. but i think it'd be better to discuss further and open another PR so this one doesnt get too big and too much out of scope.
3. currently it gets the higher playback position, i believe it can be improved but then again, it'd be best to discuss further on another issue

also, i missed having more control over playbacks, such as getting their position or loop counts individually - or even setting their position with seek individually, but for this PR i think these changes cover well its purpose
@adamscott can you take a look at this PR when you have time, please?
